name: SiteGPT
tagline: A bootstrapped, code-executing AI chatbot that went from weekend project to real recurring revenue without a dollar of outside funding.
tldr: SiteGPT is a no-code AI chatbot builder trained on your website and documents, distinguished by letting the bot run code snippets and connect directly to a database mid-conversation, not just answer from static text.

Pricing runs Starter ($59/mo, or $39/mo billed annually — 4,000 messages, 1,000 pages), Growth ($129/mo, or $79/mo annually — 10,000 messages, 10,000 pages), Scale ($429/mo, or $259/mo annually — 40,000 messages, 50,000 pages, Zendesk integration), and custom Enterprise (up to 500,000 pages, HIPAA eligibility).

Founded in 2023 by solo/bootstrapped founder Bhanu Teja P (also credited as Bhanu Teja Pasala/Pachipulusu), based in India, with no external funding — reportedly reached around $300K ARR by mid-2024 from a standing start.

Reviews show a familiar split pattern: launch-community feedback skews positive, with praise for the code-execution and database-connection features, while broader review aggregators run noticeably lower, and some reviewers report billing/account-access issues after payment.
There's a 7-day free trial, but it requires a credit card and there's no permanently-free plan — several reviewers specifically call this out as a trust barrier before committing to a paid plan.
keyFeatures: Ability to run executable code snippets and connect directly to a database from within a conversation, going beyond static content retrieval
Trains on up to 500,000 pages at the Enterprise tier, scaling from 1,000 pages on the entry Starter plan
Auto-refresh scheduling (manual on lower tiers, weekly on Scale, daily on Enterprise) to keep trained content current
Native Zendesk integration and webhook support on the Scale tier for connecting into an existing support stack
AI conversation insights and advanced analytics for reviewing what customers are actually asking
iOS app for managing chatbots and conversations on the go
API access from the Growth tier upward for embedding chatbot logic into custom applications
HIPAA eligibility and signed agreements available at the Enterprise tier for compliance-sensitive buyers

faq.question: What makes SiteGPT different from a basic website chatbot?
faq.answer: Its standout feature is the ability to execute code snippets and connect to a database mid-conversation, which reviewers specifically call out as differentiating it from chatbots that can only retrieve static trained text.

faq.question: How is SiteGPT priced?
faq.answer: Message- and page-volume tiered plans: Starter $39/mo (4,000 messages, 1,000 pages), Growth $79/mo (10,000 messages, 10,000 pages), Scale $259/mo (40,000 messages, 50,000 pages, Zendesk integration), and custom Enterprise up to 500,000 pages. Add-ons include branding removal (+$39/mo) and extra message blocks (+$39/mo per 5,000).

faq.question: Is there a free trial?
faq.answer: There's a 7-day free trial, but it requires a credit card up front and there's no permanently-free plan — multiple reviewers flag this as a barrier to trusting the product before paying, especially compared to competitors like Chatbase that offer a no-card free tier.

faq.question: Who built SiteGPT?
faq.answer: It was built by a bootstrapped, largely solo founder (credited as Bhanu Teja P) starting in 2023, growing to a reported ~$300K ARR by mid-2024 without external venture funding.

faq.question: Does SiteGPT integrate with existing helpdesk tools?
faq.answer: Yes, a native Zendesk integration and webhook support are available starting on the Scale tier ($259/mo), letting it plug into an existing support workflow rather than replace it outright.

scorecard.note: Reviewers describe it as super easy to train and integrate, with quick website-content ingestion.
The code-execution and live database connection capability is repeatedly singled out as more accurate and capable than static-retrieval competitors.
Effectively a website-widget-and-API product — no native WhatsApp, social DM, or voice channel documented.
Competitive per-message pricing at entry, but no card-free trial or permanent free plan, and add-on costs (branding removal, extra messages) add up quickly at scale.
Some reviewers report broken billing/account-access flows and weak support handoff after payment, a real concern for a bootstrapped, presumably small team.

criteriaScores.note: Beyond the website widget, SiteGPT natively connects to Slack, Facebook Messenger, Google Chat, Crisp, Zendesk, Freshdesk Messaging, and Zoho SalesIQ, but WhatsApp is explicitly listed as 'Coming soon' and there's no SMS, Instagram DM, or voice channel (sitegpt.ai/integrations, checked Aug 2026).

Escalated conversations can be replied to from the 'SiteGPT inbox' or from connected tools like Slack, Zendesk, or Crisp (sitegpt.ai/docs/introduction), but there's no documented evidence of a true single cross-channel thread per customer — it reads more like routing into existing tools than full unification.

Genuine LLM-backed agent running on GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.1-mini per sitegpt.ai's own pricing/model notes, not canned replies — corroborated by Product Hunt reviewers describing it as automating real customer-facing tasks, not scripted responses.

No independent, audited resolution-rate benchmark exists — the review base is too thin to trust. Be skeptical of any vendor-cited deflection percentage; some reviewers instead report occasional inaccurate answers requiring retraining.

Trains automatically from URLs, sitemaps, uploaded files (PDF/DOCX/CSV), YouTube videos/playlists, and cloud drives (Google Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Box, Notion, GitHub, Confluence) — no manual intent-building required (sitegpt.ai/integrations, sitegpt.ai/docs).

Lets you include/exclude specific trained pages to keep answers 'accurate and on-brand' (sitegpt.ai/features), which is a real scoping control, but there's no documented source-citation UI, and one reviewer specifically cites "occasional inaccurate answers requiring retraining and feedback loops."

The 'Functions' feature goes beyond if/then rules — it runs code and connects to a live database/API mid-conversation to screen leads, book meetings, recommend products, and answer 'where is my order' (sitegpt.ai/docs/navigating-your-chatbot/functions), and Product Hunt reviewers independently call out code-execution and database connection as the standout differentiator.

One Product Hunt reviewer specifically credits it with 'analyzing user intent' well, but no vendor-documented frustration/sentiment-flagging feature was found — evidence here is thin and largely anecdotal.

A 'SiteGPT inbox' exists for reviewing and replying to escalated conversations (sitegpt.ai/docs/introduction), but there's no evidence it unifies all channels into one single-customer view beyond routing to Slack/Zendesk/Crisp.
Documented 'Escalate to a Human' flow lets visitors hand off at any time, replyable from the SiteGPT inbox or connected tools like Slack, Zendesk, or Crisp (sitegpt.ai/docs/introduction).

Not listed among SiteGPT's native integrations (sitegpt.ai/integrations, checked Aug 2026); the generic 'Functions' API/webhook connector could theoretically be wired to Shopify with custom development, but there's no dedicated app.
Same as Shopify — not listed on sitegpt.ai/integrations. Only the generic Functions/API connector could reach WooCommerce, and only with custom setup.

Real, actively published WordPress plugin (wordpress.org/plugins/sitegpt) with one-field configuration, automatic script injection, and no-code install — a genuine native integration, not just a generic embed.
No dedicated Wix app found; SiteGPT reaches Wix sites via the same universal JavaScript embed snippet used on any website, not a native marketplace integration.
Same pattern as Wix — reachable only via the generic embed script pasted into site code; no dedicated Squarespace app found.

SiteGPT's own blog documents pasting its embed script into Webflow's site-wide custom code — functional, but it's the same generic embed used everywhere, not a native Webflow app or marketplace listing.

Webhook support (real-time events for new messages, escalations, and leads) is available on the Scale tier and up and can be pointed at Zapier, Make, or n8n, but no dedicated Zapier or Make app listing was found for SiteGPT — this is generic webhook connectivity, not native pre-built triggers/actions.

HubSpot is explicitly listed as 'Coming soon' on sitegpt.ai/integrations; no Salesforce or Pipedrive integration found anywhere. Lead capture can push to 'your inbox, webhook, or CRM' generically (per sitegpt.ai/docs), but no native CRM sync exists today.

The Functions feature can connect to a live backend/database to answer 'Where is my order?' and support instant checkout, per SiteGPT's own docs and blog — but this requires custom developer setup via API/Functions, not an out-of-box order lookup like a dedicated Shopify integration would provide.

Documented support for 95+ languages with auto language handling ('Language Support' listed at 95 languages on sitegpt.ai/features), repeated consistently across SiteGPT's own marketing and third-party aggregator coverage.

Chat History and conversation insights track resolution/escalation rate, response time, CSAT, and common questions/knowledge gaps per SiteGPT's own docs — a real feature set, but self-reported with no independent benchmarking found, and 'basic' analytics on Starter upgrades to 'advanced' only on Growth+.

Fully public per-message/per-page tiered pricing page, but genuinely confusing in practice: the commonly-cited $39/$79/$259 figures only apply if billed annually — true monthly billing is $59/$129/$429 (sitegpt.ai/pricing, verified directly) — and one reviewer notes each Q&A pair counts as messages toward the cap, roughly halving effective capacity versus a naive read of the limits.

API access from the Growth tier up, webhooks from the Scale tier up, plus a documented API reference, CLI, and MCP server support (sitegpt.ai/docs) for building custom logic on top rather than being locked into a fixed workflow builder.

pricing.model: Tiered SaaS by monthly message volume and trained page count, billed monthly or annually (annual billing is discounted roughly 34%)

pricingBreakdown: SiteGPT's ladder runs Starter ($59/mo billed monthly, or $39/mo effective if billed annually at $468/yr; 4,000 messages/1,000 pages) to Growth ($129/mo monthly, or $79/mo annually; 10,000 messages/10,000 pages) to Scale ($429/mo monthly, or $259/mo annually; 40,000 messages/50,000 pages plus the Zendesk integration) — source: sitegpt.ai/pricing, verified 2026-08-25. Unlike Chatbase, there's no free plan to use indefinitely (SiteGPT does offer a 7-day free trial with a credit card required, per sitegpt.ai/pricing, but no capped free tier), which is real friction when a Starter commitment is competing against Chatbase's $0 Free tier and $32/mo Hobby plan for a similar basic FAQ-bot use case. Where SiteGPT's pricing actually earns its premium is the code-execution and live database connection capability baked into every tier — that's not something Chatbase or Wonderchat offer at any price point, so if that capability is genuinely load-bearing for your use case, the trial-only (no free plan) structure matters a lot less. Scale sits close to Crisp's Essentials ($95/mo) and Plus ($295/mo) tiers price-wise, but buys a fundamentally different thing — a much bigger trained-content ceiling (50,000 pages) rather than more human seats or omnichannel reach, so don't compare it to Crisp on seats-per-dollar; compare it on pages-per-dollar instead, which is the metric that actually matters for a documentation-heavy site. Note also that one reviewer flagged that each question-plus-answer exchange counts as messages toward the monthly cap, which roughly halves the effective conversation capacity versus a naive read of the advertised message limits.

capabilities.note: The differentiator here is real and specific: the bot can run code snippets and query a live database mid-conversation instead of only paraphrasing crawled text, which is repeatedly the single thing reviewers point to when explaining why they chose this over a static-retrieval competitor. If your use case genuinely needs a live answer (order status, dynamic pricing logic) rather than a documented one, this capability is worth the premium over a cheaper crawl-only bot.

Training scales from 1,000 pages on Starter up to 500,000 pages on Enterprise, which is a real ceiling most competitors on this list don't approach — Chatbase and Wonderchat are built for far smaller content sets. If you're sitting on a large documentation site or knowledge base, that page ceiling alone can be the deciding factor over a cheaper, shallower competitor.

The web widget is how customers reach the bot, but there's no separate human live-chat layer built into the product — if a conversation needs a human, SiteGPT's answer is the Scale tier's native Zendesk integration, not a built-in inbox of its own. Budget for that integration if human handoff matters to you, rather than assuming it's included at lower tiers.

pros: Genuinely differentiated technical capability — running code and connecting to a live database mid-conversation, not just retrieving static text
Scales to very large trained content sets (up to 500,000 pages on Enterprise), suited to large documentation-heavy sites
Native Zendesk integration and webhooks make it easier to slot into an existing support stack rather than replace it
Bootstrapped, profitable-trending company history suggests a founder incentivized to keep the product working, not chase a growth-at-all-costs exit
cons: No permanently-free plan and the 7-day trial requires a credit card, which multiple reviewers specifically cite as a reason they hesitated to buy
No native messaging channels beyond the website widget and API — no WhatsApp, social DM, or voice
Some reviewers report billing and account-access problems after paying, plus weaker support handoff than larger competitors
Add-on costs (branding removal, extra message blocks) stack onto already-tiered pricing, complicating total cost

sentiment.quote: SiteGPT is much better in terms of features...the only chatbot that allows automating customer facing tasks by letting me run code snippets and connect to my database
It's super easy to train and integrate. Moreover, I was able to add executionary functions
I paid for the essential plan but don't have access to creating any chatbot

bestFor: Technical teams that want a chatbot capable of executing code or querying a live database, not just answering FAQs
Large content sites needing to train on tens or hundreds of thousands of pages
Businesses already using Zendesk that want an AI layer bolted onto that existing workflow
Buyers comfortable providing a card for the 7-day trial, without a permanently-free plan, based on documented feature depth
verdict: SiteGPT's code-execution and live-database-connection capability is a real, specific technical edge over most website-widget chatbots on this list — it's the difference between a bot that can actually look something up right now versus one that paraphrases a page crawled last week. That's worth paying for if it's load-bearing for your use case, but be honest with yourself about whether it actually is: if you just need a straightforward FAQ bot, you're paying at least $39/mo (billed annually; $59/mo monthly) for a capability you won't use when Chatbase gives you a free tier to start with instead. The lack of a no-card free trial is the specific friction point I'd flag hardest — SiteGPT's 7-day trial still requires a credit card up front, a real trust gap next to competitors who let you kick the tires before paying, and it's compounded by Product Hunt reports of paying customers losing access to their chatbot after payment, which is the kind of concrete, specific complaint that matters more than a star rating ever does. My honest take: worth a serious look if the code-execution feature is genuinely the reason you're here and you're comfortable handing over a card for the trial without a permanently-free plan. Skip it if you're chasing a basic FAQ bot — that's a solved problem elsewhere, with better trial options and less risk.
